name: Default Repo Template + .md Governance
description: What should a default Claude Code repo look like? The template has five distinct layers that each need a community-validated default: (1) .md governance, (2) hooks, (3) skills, (4) subagent profiles, (5) other conventions.

md_governance.description: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / DESIGN.md structure: what rules, constraints, and context ship by default. How verbose vs. concise. What sections are mandatory. Community converging on a three-layer pattern.
approaches: Three-layer pattern (emerging community standard): CLAUDE.md (behavioral rules/prohibitions) + DESIGN.md (visual design system, Google Labs format) + SKILL.md (reusable procedures). Reference DESIGN.md from CLAUDE.md: 'Always refer to DESIGN.md when generating UI components.'
Official: concise CLAUDE.md checked into git, /init to bootstrap then refine. Remove any line that wouldn't cause mistakes if deleted.
gstack: CLAUDE.md acts as a router — delegates to specialist skill roles rather than containing all rules inline
Karpathy LLM wiki: wiki/ directory maintained by the agent provides living cross-session memory alongside CLAUDE.md
DESIGN.md (Google Labs, April 2026, 11.6k+ stars): design-token YAML + prose rationale in one file. CLI lints WCAG AA contrast, exports to Tailwind/DTCG.

hooks.description: Shell commands that fire on Claude Code events (pre/post tool use, session start/stop). What hooks should ship by default for safety and observability?
approaches: disler/claude-code-hooks-mastery: canonical reference for all 12 lifecycle events with build/validate orchestration patterns
Intercom (Brian Scanlan): production-safe DB hooks (read-replica only, block critical tables, Okta auth, DynamoDB audit trail)
Matt Pocock git-guardrails-claude-code skill: hook-style block on dangerous git commands
Clinejection (March 2026, Adnan Khan): demonstrates prompt injection via malicious GitHub issue titles in claude-code-action workflow — hooks on tool/git/PR boundaries are now table-stakes for CI use
hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code: curated hook examples registry

skills.description: Which slash-command skills to include out of the box. How to author them. How to version and share them.
approaches: Skills > imperative code (David Gomes / Cursor, AIE Europe 2026): replacing 12K LoC with a 200 LoC SKILL.md as the new normal — write skills, not code
Matt Pocock /skills repo (61k+ stars, May 2026): 17 production workflow skills published from his own .claude/ directory
Addy Osmani agent-skills (28k+, Feb 2026): full SDLC skills bundle (Define-Plan-Build-Verify-Review-Ship) with reusable personas
wshobson/agents (34k+): pre-built subagent team for full-stack web (backend-architect, frontend-developer, test-automator, security-auditor, deployment-engineer)
gstack (89k+): 23 specialist skills covering CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, Release Manager, QA, Security, Doc Engineer roles
Marc Klingen (Langfuse, AIE Europe 2026): 'Skill issue' — practical pitfalls of writing SKILL.md that teaches a coding agent to use a specific library
Pedro Rodrigues (Supabase, AIE Europe 2026): skills + MCP are complementary (skills = static knowledge, MCP = live tools); design them together
Matt Pocock: /grill-me (structured intake), /write-a-prd, /write-issues (plan-mode enforcement)
hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code: community-curated registry of validated skills

subagent_profiles.description: How to define and configure subagents: their personas, constraints, allowed tools, context they receive. What subagent profiles should exist in a default template?
approaches: gstack model: named specialist roles (CEO = strategy, Designer = UI/UX, QA = test coverage) each with their own skill file and implicit persona
Sandcastle model: sandbox-isolated agents with Docker + git worktrees, pluggable local or remote

other.description: Other conventions: directory structure, gitignore defaults, memory patterns, CI integration, token budget guidance.

approaches: gstack pattern: 23-skill configuration with specialist roles (CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, etc.)
Karpathy LLM wiki pattern: raw/ + wiki/ + schema/ three-layer architecture
Official best practice: concise CLAUDE.md checked into git, /init to bootstrap then refine

name: Claude Code Skills
description: Which skills to include in a default setup. How to author them. Community-shared skill registries.
approaches: gstack: 23 specialist skills (CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, Release Manager, QA, Security, Doc Engineer roles)
Matt Pocock: /grill-me, /write-a-prd, /write-issues for plan-mode enforcement
hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code: curated community registry
aihero.dev skills repo: Matt Pocock's personal .claude/ directory published

name: Session Management / Context Compaction
description: Claude's default context compaction loses state badly. Current best practice (Matt Pocock): backup context at ~100k tokens, /clear, reload backup. Need to verify if this fully solves context collapse or if additional structure is required.
approaches: Token-efficiency primitives (May 2026): caveman (54k stars, terse-prompting style — ~65% output token cut), zilliztech/claude-context (10k, BM25+vector code search MCP — 40% reduction), yvgude/lean-ctx (1k, Context-OS shell hooks — 60-95% cut). Orthogonal strategies; pick at least one for any long-running session.
backup-clear-reload at ~100k tokens (Matt Pocock / Sandcastle)
Intervene at ~60% context utilization; auto-compact triggers at ~80-90%
/compact with specific instructions ('Focus on the API changes') for better summaries
Session Memory writes summaries continuously — /compact is now near-instant
Karpathy LLM wiki pattern: wiki/ directory updated by agent provides cross-session memory
Cavemem (Julius Brussee): cross-agent persistent memory layer using compressed-grammar storage
claude-code-transcripts (Simon Willison): export sessions to HTML/Gist for reference

name: Low-Level Frontend Verification
description: Claude will claim a UI change is live when it isn't. Need reliable verification via Playwright, Chromium, or similar that a change is actually rendered correctly.
approaches: Playwright MCP server (executeautomation/mcp-playwright) — exposes browser automation to Claude Code via MCP
Claude in Chrome — for day-to-day dev/debug
Playwright MCP for pre-release test suite verification
Microsoft Playwright CLI — ~4x fewer tokens than full accessibility tree streaming

name: Robust Testing / TDD Workflow
description: When are tests first created? How does a default template manage test-driven development across iterative FE work vs. large feature merges? How does Claude stay in sync with the test suite?
approaches: Red/green/refactor loop — be explicit with Claude that you are doing TDD to prevent premature mock implementations
Simon Willison's TDD pattern: tests as built-in success conditions that both developer and agent can verify
Matt Pocock's /grill-me before implementation to prevent premature coding

name: Design Systems
description: Default Claude doesn't guide toward a design system. Need: how is a design system standardized/defined? What is the default web app design system? How do we customize it?
approaches: DESIGN.md (Google Labs, April 2026): single markdown file at repo root with YAML design tokens + prose rationale. AI agents read it as persistent context. Exports to Tailwind or W3C DTCG tokens.json. Community-standard three-layer pattern: CLAUDE.md (behavior) + DESIGN.md (visuals) + SKILL.md (procedures).
awesome-design-md (VoltAgent, 71k+ stars): 100+ pre-built DESIGN.md files for popular brands/systems — starting point for any project
paper.design (Stephen Haney): code-native canvas on real React + Tailwind. Designers get production-ready components. Complements DESIGN.md at the component layer.

name: Design Toolbar / Fast UI Iteration
description: Need to: (1) view design system tokens/primitives/components, (2) add to it, (3) navigate pages, (4) see viewports, (5) fast-iterate on UI similar to element inspector + claude.ai/design comment-on-element. Could be split: design system viewer + design toolbar.
approaches: Open Design (nexu-io, 27.9k stars, May 2026): local-first open-source Claude Design alternative. Auto-detects 15+ coding-agent CLIs and uses them as design engines. Ships 129 design systems as DESIGN.md, 31 SKILL.md skills, exposes MCP server so Claude Code in any other repo can query live tokens.

design-extract (Manavarya09, ~2k stars, Apr 2026): Playwright-driven extractor that turns any live website into DTCG tokens, Tailwind v4 config, shadcn/ui components, Figma variables — exposed as MCP server
paper.design (Stephen Haney): code-native canvas on real React + Tailwind
claude.ai/design comment-on-element as reference UX
Open Design YouTube series (8XcbyliBwc4 etc.) — practitioner walkthroughs of the workflow

name: Unified UX Layer Across Projects
description: A unified interface: see async tasks running across all projects, switch between projects, unified chat (Figma Make / claude.ai/design style), drill into specific agent sessions, cross-device (Mac, PC, mobile), cloud-persisted auth and integrations (GitHub, Neon, Render, etc.).

name: MCP Servers for Claude Code
description: Which Model Context Protocol servers are most useful for Claude Code subscription users building web apps? How do you configure them? Which are stable enough to ship by default in a project template?
approaches: Playwright MCP (executeautomation/mcp-playwright): browser automation + visual verification — the highest-value MCP for web app development
claude-context (zilliztech, ~10.7k): BM25 + dense vector + AST chunking MCP for searching big monorepos efficiently — ~40% token reduction
design-extract MCP (Manavarya09, Apr 2026): exposes a 'extract design system from live URL' tool to Claude Code
Open Design MCP (nexu-io): exposes live design tokens / CSS / components from your design repo to any Claude Code session
designmd.ai MCP: direct DESIGN.md file integration without manual file downloads
Ruflo ships 314 native MCP tools — source for discovering new MCPs in the agent orchestration space
Pedro Rodrigues (Supabase, AIE Europe 2026): pair skills (static knowledge) with MCP (live tools) — design them together
CLAUDE.md pattern: list active MCPs and their purpose in the project root so Claude always knows what tools are available

name: Multi-Agent Orchestration
description: Patterns for running multiple Claude Code agents in parallel: shared task lists, worktree isolation, dependency tracking, merge strategies.
approaches: Claude Agent Teams (built-in): team lead coordinates, teammates work in own context windows and communicate directly
Subagents: isolated parallel workers that report back (no direct coordination)
Conductor (macOS app): isolated git worktree workspaces with real-time visibility and diff review
Vibe Kanban: cross-agent orchestration with kanban planning and built-in browser preview
Ruflo/Claude Flow: enterprise-grade swarms with federated cross-machine comms and self-learning memory
Sandcastle: git worktrees + Docker isolation for truly AFK agent runs
Decision rule: only use multi-agent when phases are genuinely asynchronous or need different specialists
